363	     7	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
364	     8	
365	     9	There are two ways to restyle captions, depending on what you want to change. A word style and its looks are set when the captions are generated, so changing those means generating again. Font, outline and backdrop are ordinary text settings, which you can change on a run of captions in the inspector.
366	    10	
367	    11	<AtAGlance
368	    12	  menu="File ▸ Generate Captions…"
369	    13	  where={['The Generate Captions sheet ▸ Replace:', 'Clip tab ▸ Text']}
370	    14	  tools={['transcribe', 'set_text']}
371	    15	/>
372	    16	
373	    17	## Restyle by generating again
374	    18	
375	    19	<Steps>
376	    20	
377	    21	1. Choose **File ▸ Generate Captions…** and set **From:** to the same clips.
378	    22	
379	    23	2. Choose the new word style and [looks](/captions/word-caption-looks/).
380	    24	
381	    25	3. Tick **Replace: existing captions**. The line under it names each track it will remove, with its caption count, for example "Replaces “Captions” (12 captions)."
382	    26	
383	    27	4. Choose **Generate**.
384	    28	
385	    29	</Steps>
386	    30	
387	    31	The old tracks are removed and the new one takes their place at the front of the stack, all in one undo step, **Generate Captions**. The new track takes the first free name, so a lone **Captions** track is replaced by another called **Captions**.
388	    32	
389	    33	What it costs depends on the engine:
390	    34	
391	    35	- **AssemblyAI:** the cached transcript is reused whatever style you ask for, so nothing is uploaded and nothing is billed. That holds while the language, **Speakers:** and **Vocabulary:** match the transcript and **Transcribe again:** stays unticked. See [Transcribe with AssemblyAI](/captions/assemblyai-transcription/).
392	    36	- **On this Mac:** the audio is recognised again. It's free, but it takes the time again.
393	    37	
394	    38	:::caution
395	    39	New pages are made from the transcript, not from the old track. Words you corrected, pages you split or trimmed, and anything you restyled by hand go with the old track. To page a track again and keep your corrections, use [Re-lay Captions](/captions/re-lay-captions/) instead.
396	    40	:::
397	    41	
398	    42	## Which tracks Replace may remove
399	    43	
400	    44	**Replace:** is live only for a word style, and only when there's a track it may replace. It's greyed out with Subtitles chosen. When it isn't live, it's unticked and the line under it is hidden.
401	    45	
402	    46	A track qualifies when:
403	    47	
404	    48	- it's named **Captions** or **Captions N**, such as **Captions 2**. A track you renamed doesn't qualify.
405	    49	- it holds at least one clip, and only text clips.
406	    50	- every one of those clips overlaps a clip being transcribed.
407	    51	
408	    52	The last rule is about the whole track. If even one caption on it sits outside what **From:** covers, the track is left alone and **Replace:** won't list it. Choosing a wider **From:** can bring it in.
409	    53	
410	    54	The old track's style doesn't matter, so **Replace:** also swaps out a Subtitles track or an [imported](/captions/import-captions/) one that meets these rules.
411	    55	
412	    56	## Change a run of captions together
413	    57	
414	    58	To change how captions look without changing their style, select them and use the inspector.
415	    59	
416	    60	<Steps>
417	    61	
418	    62	1. [Select the captions](/timeline/selecting-clips/) on the timeline.
419	    63	
420	    64	2. Open the **Clip** tab and its **Text** sub-tab.
421	    65	
422	    66	3. Change what you need under [**Font**, **Style**](/text-and-shapes/text-style/), [**Outline**, **Backdrop**](/text-and-shapes/text-outline-and-backdrop/) or [**Box**](/text-and-shapes/text-box/).
423	    67	
424	    68	</Steps>
425	    69	
426	    70	Each page keeps its own words and word timing. Its word style stays too: the highlight colour, the pop and the pill only change by generating again, or through an agent. See [Word colours](/captions/word-caption-looks/#word-colours).
427	    71	
428	    72	:::note
429	    73	A change of typeface on a word caption page, which a text preset also makes, means Re-lay Captions no longer recognises its track and [keeps it as placed](/captions/re-lay-captions/#tracks-kept-as-placed).
430	    74	:::
431	    75	
432	    76	## Good to know
433	    77	
434	    78	- **Replace:** always opens unticked. The sheet doesn't remember it.
435	    79	- A hidden or locked caption track is replaced like any other, and the new track is visible and unlocked.
436	    80	- If you cancel a run, nothing is placed and the old tracks stay.
437	    81	- If one file can't be transcribed, the captions from the other files are still placed and the old tracks still go, so the captions over that file's clips are lost. Undo brings them back.
438	    82	- To go from a word style back to Subtitles, generate the Subtitles track, then [remove the old one](/timeline/manage-tracks/). **Replace:** isn't available for that.
439	    83	- With a [nest](/editing/nests/) open, the sheet works on that nest's tracks.
440	    84	
441	    85	## With an agent
442	    86	
443	    87	`transcribe` restyles the same way, as long as it asks for a word style and places the captions. An agent can also change a placed page's word style directly with `set_text`, which keeps your corrected words. See [Word colours](/captions/word-caption-looks/#with-an-agent).
444	    88	
445	    89	## Related
446	    90	
447	    91	- [Word caption styles](/captions/word-caption-styles/)
448	    92	- [Looks for word captions](/captions/word-caption-looks/)
449	    93	- [Edit captions](/captions/edit-captions/)

451	=== re-lay-captions
452	     1	---
453	     2	title: Re-lay captions for a canvas
454	     3	description: Page word captions again after a canvas size change, keeping every word you corrected, and find out why a track was left as it was.
455	     4	---
456	     5	
457	     6	import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
458	     7	import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
459	     8	
460	     9	Word captions are paged for the canvas they were made on, so a narrower canvas can leave them too wide. Re-lay Captions pages them again for the new width, from the words they already hold.
461	    10	
462	    11	<AtAGlance menu="File ▸ Re-lay Captions for This Canvas" tools="relay_captions" />
463	    12	
464	    13	## Re-lay Captions for This Canvas
465	    14	
466	    15	<Steps>
467	    16	
468	    17	1. [Change the canvas size](/projects/canvas-size/) on the Document tab.
469	    18	
470	    19	2. Choose **File ▸ Re-lay Captions for This Canvas**. It has no keyboard shortcut and no options.
471	    20	
472	    21	3. If a sheet appears, read which tracks were [kept as placed](#tracks-kept-as-placed) and why.
473	    22	
474	    23	</Steps>
475	    24	
476	    25	Frame Job looks at every track named **Captions** or **Captions N** that holds only text clips. A track whose pages are all in one of the five [word styles](/captions/word-caption-styles/), with the same [looks](/captions/word-caption-looks/), is paged again from the words its pages hold. Nothing is transcribed again, so nothing is uploaded or billed.
477	    26	
478	    27	The whole re-lay is one undo step, **Re-lay Captions**.
479	    28	
480	    29	## What a re-lay keeps
481	    30	
482	    31	Every correction you typed is kept, because the new pages are made from the words on the old ones.
483	    32	
484	    33	Each page is paged again inside its own clip, and the new pages take the old track's place:
485	    34	
486	    35	- A page you split, trimmed or moved keeps its words where they are.
487	    36	- Pages are never merged across clips. A re-lay can split a page that's too wide for the new canvas, but a wider canvas won't join short pages together.
488	    37	- Words cut off by a trim stay cut off.
489	    38	- The new pages go on a track with the same name, in the same place in the track stack, hidden and locked if the old one was.
490	    39	
491	    40	The new pages are drawn fresh from the style, so any other change you made to a page goes. That includes a colour, an outline, a size, a position, or an unticked **UPPERCASE**.
492	    41	
493	    42	## Tracks kept as placed
494	    43	
495	    44	A track that can't be re-laid stays exactly as it was. A sheet after the edit names each one and why, under a first line that reads "Re-laid 2 caption tracks for this canvas." or "No caption track was re-laid."
496	    45	
497	    46	Each track gets a line like this:
498	    47	
499	    48	> Caption track "Captions 2" is kept as placed: it holds a page with no word timings.
500	    49	
501	    50	| The reason | What it means |
502	    51	| --- | --- |
503	    52	| it is a matte track | The track is a [matte track](/canvas/matte-tracks/). |
504	    53	| it holds a page with no word timings | It's a [Subtitles](/captions/subtitles/) or imported track, or a page lost its timing because you [changed its number of words](/captions/edit-captions/). |
505	    54	| it holds a page none of whose words starts inside it | A trim or split left a page with no word that begins on it. |
506	    55	| it holds a page in a style Frame Job does not make | You changed a page's font, or an agent changed its word style. |
507	    56	| its pages are in more than one style | Pages on the track differ in style or looks, for example after you moved some from another track. |
508	    57	| *N* captions is more than this project has room for | The new pages would take the project past its limit of 4,096 clips. The sentence says how many more would fit. |
509	    58	
510	    59	No sheet appears when every track was re-laid.
511	    60	
512	    61	To re-wrap a Subtitles track, or a track that lost its timing, generate it again on the new canvas. See [Restyle a caption track](/captions/restyle-captions/).
513	    62	
514	    63	## When it is available, and inside a nest
515	    64	
516	    65	The item is greyed out when:
517	    66	
518	    67	- there's no caption track it can re-lay
519	    68	- a sheet is open
520	    69	- a recording is running
521	    70	
522	    71	So if one of the first five reasons in the table above rules out every caption track, the item is greyed out and no sheet tells you why.
523	    72	
524	    73	Inside a [nest](/editing/nests/), it works on the nest's tracks at the nest's size.
525	    74	
526	    75	**File ▸ Make Vertical Version…** does the same for the vertical copy. See [What Make Vertical changes](/framing/vertical-what-changes/).
527	    76	
528	    77	## Good to know
529	    78	
530	    79	- A track with any other name isn't looked at, and the sheet doesn't mention it. Neither is a track that holds a clip other than text.
531	    80	- The item doesn't check whether the canvas changed. Choosing it on the same canvas pages the track again, which still drops the hand changes listed in [What a re-lay keeps](#what-a-re-lay-keeps). Undo brings them back.
532	    81	
533	    82	## With an agent
534	    83	
535	    84	`relay_captions` does the same in the timeline or nest that's open. When nothing can be re-laid, it answers with each kept track and its reason, so an agent can tell you why the menu item is greyed out. See [Tools: captions and transcripts](/mcp/tools-captions/).
536	    85	
537	    86	## Related
538	    87

540	    89	- [Word caption styles](/captions/word-caption-styles/)

     1	import Foundation
     2	
     3	/// Word-caption PAGES (road map 8 §5c, W4a): recognised words in, one
     4	/// `CaptionLayout.Cue` per page out, each carrying its `words` — for every
     5	/// caption style but Subtitles, whose cues stay `CaptionCues.build`'s,
     6	/// unchanged and byte-identical (spec §11 W-7).
     7	///
     8	/// **A page is filled to a MEASURED width, not a count.** The width test is
     9	/// `LayerRenderers.measuredSize(for:)` of the page exactly as it will be
    10	/// placed — the style's face, size, case, outline and word-style headroom —
    11	/// against `widthBudget` of the canvas width. That function is static and
    12	/// lock-guarded, so this runs on whatever thread the engine runs on
    13	/// (`Transcriber.work`, `CloudTranscriber.work`, the server thread).
    14	///
    15	/// **A page is confined to its job's span** (spec §11 W-7). `lead` shifts a
    16	/// word and `hold` extends a page, and neither may carry a page past
    17	/// `span.upperBound`: every word is clamped into the span after `lead`, a
    18	/// word pushed off the end sits on the clip's LAST FRAME (`upper − frame`,
    19	/// because the core snaps to the NEAREST frame and one tick short of the
    20	/// bound would land on the next clip's first frame), and the last page ends
    21	/// at or before the bound. So pages of two abutting clips abut at most, and
    22	/// `CaptionLayout.place`'s trim pass never fires on a transcript —
    23	/// `CaptionCues`' promise, kept here too.
    24	///
    25	/// **The row never blinks.** A page ends at `min(next.start, last.end +
    26	/// hold)`, and where the gap to the next page is under `breakGap` it ends AT
    27	/// the next page's start. That is `CaptionCues`' one-frame gap deliberately
    28	/// not applied: abutting clips place cleanly (`b.start == a.end` is not an
    29	/// overlap).
    30	///
    31	/// **Pauses are word gaps and punctuation** (W4a's decision, spec §11
    32	/// W-7): a gap of `breakGap` or more, or a word ending `.?!…`, closes a
    33	/// page. `SilenceDetector`/`MediaSpeech` are not consulted — this is pure
    34	/// arithmetic over the words, testable with no audio (road map 8 §10.9).
    35	enum CaptionPages {
    36	
    37	    /// Road map 8 §8's numbers, in ticks where they are times.
    38	    struct Rules: Equatable {
    39	        /// Of the canvas width.
    40	        var widthBudget = 0.86
    41	        /// Of the style's size: where a lone word stops shrinking and wraps.
    42	        var shrinkFloor = 0.80
    43	        /// A width break within this many words after a `,;:` moves back.
    44	        var clauseWindow = 2
    45	        /// …if the page before the mark is at least this much of the budget.
    46	        var clauseMinimum = 0.5
    47	        /// 3 s on screen, to the last word's end.
    48	        var maxLength: Ticks = 1_800_000
    49	        /// 0.25 s: a gap this long closes a page (W0 q1's measurement).
    50	        var breakGap: Ticks = 150_000
    51	        /// 0.5 s a page stays up after its last word.
    52	        var hold: Ticks = 300_000
    53	
    54	        static let standard = Rules()
    55	    }
    56	
    57	    /// What a run asks the pager for: the style and the canvas it measures
    58	    /// against. A DISPLAY choice — never part of a transcript's cache key
    59	    /// (spec §11 R6-15).
    60	    struct Request: Equatable {
    61	        let style: CaptionStyle
    62	        let canvas: CGSize
    63	    }
    64	
    65	    /// Where each engine's word starts sit against the voice, as a shift
    66	    /// applied in `normalize` — road map 8 §8, MEASURED by W0 q2: on-device
    67	    /// runs 270 ms EARLY (+162 000 ticks), AssemblyAI 60 ms LATE (−36 000).
    68	    /// It lives here and nowhere else; `CaptionCues` never shifts a word.
    69	    static func lead(for engine: TranscriptionEngine) -> Ticks {
    70	        switch engine {
    71	        case .apple: return 162_000
    72	        case .assemblyai: return -36_000
    73	        }
    74	    }
    75	
    76	    /// The words the pager reads: trimmed, empties dropped, a word with
    77	    /// internal whitespace split into tokens sharing its timing, sorted by
    78	    /// start (ties in arrival order), shifted by `lead`, then clamped into
    79	    /// `span` — start into `[lower, upper − frame]`, end into `[start,
    80	    /// upper]`.
    81	    static func normalize(
    82	        _ words: [CaptionCues.Word], lead: Ticks, span: Range<Ticks>, frame: Ticks
    83	    ) -> [CaptionCues.Word] {
    84	        var tokens: [(order: Int, word: CaptionCues.Word)] = []
    85	        for word in words {
    86	            for piece in word.text.split(whereSeparator: \.isWhitespace) {
    87	                tokens.append((
    88	                    tokens.count,
    89	                    CaptionCues.Word(
    90	                        text: String(piece), start: word.start, end: word.end,
    91	                        speaker: word.speaker)
    92	                ))
    93	            }
    94	        }
    95	        tokens.sort {
    96	            $0.word.start == $1.word.start ? $0.order < $1.order : $0.word.start < $1.word.start
    97	        }
    98	        let lower = span.lowerBound
    99	        let upper = span.upperBound
   100	        let lastFrame = max(lower, upper - frame)
   101	        return tokens.map { entry in
   102	            let word = entry.word
   103	            let start = min(max(word.start + lead, lower), lastFrame)
   104	            let end = min(max(word.end + lead, start), upper)
   105	            return CaptionCues.Word(text: word.text, start: start, end: end, speaker: word.speaker)
   106	        }
   107	    }
   108	
   109	    /// Whether `content` — one line, or lines split at `"\n"`, each tested
   110	    /// alone — lays within `budget` pixels in `style` at `size`.
   111	    static func fits(_ content: String, style: CaptionStyle, size: Double, budget: Double) -> Bool {
   112	        content.split(separator: "\n").allSatisfy { width(String($0), style, size) <= budget }
   113	    }
   114	
   115	    /// The Subtitles-or-pages dispatch both engines call per job.
   116	    /// `.subtitles` is `CaptionCues.build`, untouched: no `lead`, no span.
   117	    static func cues(
   118	        from words: [CaptionCues.Word], span: Range<Ticks>, frame: Ticks, request: Request,
   119	        engine: TranscriptionEngine, clip: UInt32?, media: UInt32? = nil
   120	    ) -> [CaptionLayout.Cue] {
   121	        guard request.style.isWordStyle else {
   122	            return CaptionCues.build(from: words, frame: frame, clip: clip, media: media)
   123	        }
   124	        return build(
   125	            from: words, span: span, frame: frame, request: request, engine: engine, clip: clip)
   126	    }
